Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Household, washing & chores

sort verb

put in order by kind

also sort into, sort through, separate out, arrange

classical

Ov. Met. 14.266–267: sparsōsque sine ōrdine flōrēs sēcernunt calathīs
Col. 12.50.1: lēctāsque crībrāre et sēcernere
Varr. RR 2.2.13 (Lewis & Short)

sēcernō, sēcernere, sēcrēvī, sēcrētum

verb, third conjugation; from what, ab or the ablative

sort out, separate, set apart

Sorting as separating: the good from the bad, one kind from another, each into its basket.

Other words

  • dīgerō, dīgerere, dīgessī, dīgestum — arrange, set in order, distribute

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.1.23: dīligentissimē lēgī et dīgessī (Lewis & Short); Ov. F. 1.27: tempora dīgereret

    Sorting as putting in order: papers, books, a library (Suet., Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • grāmina dispōnunt sparsōsque sine ōrdine flōrēs sēcernunt calathīs variāsque colōribus herbās

    they lay out the plants, and sort into baskets the flowers strewn anyhow and the herbs of different coloursOv. Met. 14.266–267

  • lēctāsque crībrāre et sēcernere, quaecumque maculōsae, vitiōsae minōrisve incrēmentī vidēbuntur

    and to sieve the picked olives and sort out any that look spotted, damaged or undersizedCol. 12.50.1

See also separate, kind.

SourcesLewis & Short: secerno · Lewis & Short: digero
